answer: In a Wesolowski VDF, each identity is checked by a chain of dependent modular squarings: the next step cannot begin before the previous result exists. An attacker may run cloned identities on separate GPUs, but cannot parallelize away the required sequential work or shorten each clone’s delay, making mass Sybil creation costly in real time. A crystal-clear proof can be verified quickly; the meadow of clones still faces the same bottleneck, not a hollow claim of parallel resistance.
